episode_title: Stop Being Ghosted. Get Replies. Close Deals.

real_qa.q: Why do sales professionals get ghosted after presenting proposals without discussing price first?
real_qa.r: When you leave a meeting to create a proposal before discussing money, clients often receive it and think it is way more expensive than expected, then ghost you because they are too nice to say no. You should get agreement on a ballpark figure before leaving the meeting. For example, saying something around three to five grand a month and asking if that range makes sense helps set proper expectations and prevents ghosting.
real_qa.requete: how to avoid ghosting after sales proposal

real_qa.q: What is the difference between asking a prospect's budget and discussing realistic spending to solve their problem?
real_qa.r: Asking what is your budget gives you their impression of what it will take to solve a problem, but you know the reality of what it actually costs to be competitive in that category. The reality might be ten times more expensive than what the customer thinks. Instead of asking budget, talk about other customers you have solved problems for and ask what it would be worth to them to solve that problem, which reveals if they are realistic about actual costs.
real_qa.requete: how to discuss pricing without asking budget

real_qa.q: How should sales professionals schedule follow-up meetings to prevent cancellations?
real_qa.r: Schedule follow-up meetings to be very short and look like a small meeting on the calendar so prospects are unlikely to cancel them. If it takes more effort to cancel the meeting than to just attend it, most people will show up. A sixty-minute follow-up meeting is more likely to be canceled than a very brief five-minute meeting on the calendar.
real_qa.requete: how to prevent meeting cancellations sales

real_qa.q: Why should sales professionals request phone calls instead of Zoom meetings during prospecting?
real_qa.r: Many prospects prefer a brief five-minute phone call over a Zoom call because phone calls are non-threatening and do not require preparation, unlike Zoom which requires being in a quiet place and looking presentable. Phone calls can be taken anywhere, including at the beach, on the bus, or in the bathroom. People have better success asking for a quick phone call and then moving to something bigger rather than starting with a demanding Zoom meeting.
real_qa.requete: phone call vs zoom prospecting sales

real_qa.q: How can sales professionals use CRM reporting to identify hidden revenue opportunities?
real_qa.r: Access the reporting suite inside your CRM tool to pull custom reports that identify missing revenue gaps, clients overlooked, and year-to-year or quarter-to-quarter spending comparisons. One example identified four accounts worth over thirty thousand dollars that were being overlooked by accident. If your CRM has an AI bot or agent built in, ask it to help run a report to identify those revenue gaps and honey holes you might have missed.
